description: L’objet de l'accord cadre porte sur la fourniture d’instruments météorologiques et prestations associées au profit des centres appartenant à la Direction de l’Ingénierie et de l’Expertise (DIE) de direction générale de l’armement. Il s'agit d'un accord­-cadre composite mono­-attributaire, composé de deux parties : Une part à bons de commande conformément aux dispositions de l’article R.2362-8 au Code de la Commande Publique (CCP) et une part à marchés subséquents conformément aux articles R.2362-1 à R.2362-7 du CCP. Pour la part à bons de commandes : la fourniture, l’installation, la mise en service et formation et d’instruments météorologiques et leur maintien en condition opérationnelle Les prestations qui pourront être réalisées dans le cadre de ce présent projet d’accord­-cadre sont notamment : Famille 1: Mesure de la température. Famille 2 : Mesure de la pression atmosphérique. Famille 3 : Mesure de l’humidité, Famille 4 : Mesure du vent en surface Famille 5 : Mesure des précipitations Famille 6 : Mesure du rayonnement Famille 7 : Mesure de la visibilité Famille 8 : Observation du temps présent et passé et de l’état du sol, Famille 9 : Observation et mesure des propriétés des nuages Famille 10 : Accessoires Les marchés subséquents préciseront certaines prestations ou fournitures ultérieures, dont les caractéristiques et les modalités d’exécution sont non définies dans l’accord-cadre. Les prestations seront réalisées au profit de : DGA Essais de missiles Site Gironde : Saint¬ Médard en­ Jalles (33), DGA Essais de missiles Site Landes : Biscarrosse (40),DGA Essais de missiles Site Méditerranée Toulon, Levant et Coudon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Toulon (83), DGA Techniques navales Site de Brest (29), DGA Essais de missiles Bâtiment d’Essais et de Mesures Monge, DGA Essais de missiles Station d’Essais et de Mesures de Quimper (29), DGA Essais de missiles Station d'Essais de Mesures d'Hourtin (SEMH) (33), DGA Essais propulseurs : Saclay (91), DGA Maîtrise de l'information : Bruz (35), DGA Essais en vol Site de Cazaux (33), DGA Essais en vol Site d’Istres (13), DGA Maîtrise NRBC : Vert Le Petit (91), DGA Techniques aérospatiales : Balma (31), DGA Techniques hydrodynamiques : Val de Reuil (27), DGA Techniques terrestres Site de Bourges (18), DGA Techniques terrestres Site d’Angers (49). La date limite de remise des candidatures est fixée au 12/11/2026 à 16:00 heures (Heure de Paris). La date et l'heure limites inscrites à la rubrique 5.1.12 sont au format UTC. Il s'agit d'un Marché de défense ou de sécurité. Le présent projet de marché fait l'objet d'une procédure formalisée négociée avec mise en concurrence et publicité préalable, conformément aux dispositions des articles L.2324-1, L.2324-3, R.2324-1, R.2324-3, et R.2361-8 à R.2361-12 du CCP. L'accord-­cadre est conclu pour une durée de validité de 7 (sept) ans. Le montant maximum s'élève à 7 000 000 € HT, indiqués à la rubrique 2.1.3 ci­-après. Ce montant maximum correspond à une estimation globale pour le projet d'accord­-cadre, sans engagement de la part de l'État de l'atteindre. Le montant maximum indiqué en rubriques 2 et 5 ci-après est en euros hors taxe. Les candidats doivent indiquer dans leur candidature s'ils se présentent en tant que candidat individuel ou groupement d'opérateurs économiques. Il est interdit aux candidats de présenter pour l'accord­-cadre plusieurs offres en agissant à la fois : 1. en qualité de candidats individuels et de membres d'un ou plusieurs groupements ; 2. en qualité de membres de plusieurs groupements. La forme du groupement n'est pas imposée. La composition des groupements peut être modifiée, et il est possible d'en constituer de nouveaux entre la remise des candidatures et la remise des offres initiales si tous les membres du nouveau groupement, présenté au stade des offres, ont été autorisés au stade des candidatures à présenter une offre ou à y participer, au moins en tant que sous-contractant accepté dans la phase candidature. Le groupement nouvellement constitué doit respecter les exigences relatives aux capacités des candidats. De plus, les dispositions des articles R.2142-23 et R.2342-14 du CCP s’appliquent. La fourniture de tous les éléments/documents listés en rubriques 2.1.6 et 5.1.9 est primordiale, sous peine de rejet de la candidature de l’opérateur économique. Le présent avis de marché ne concerne que la PHASE CANDIDATURE. Le dossier de consultation sera envoyé ultérieurement aux candidats admis à soumissionner. Il pourra être fait application des dispositions de l'article R.2394-1 du CCP (clauses de réexamen relative aux conditions de variation des prix, à des évolutions, aux références des instruments de météorologie, aux situations de crise et rajout de sites bénéficiaires).

title: MatLAB Software License renewals
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE, NOT A REQUEST FOR A QUOTE (RFQ). A RFQ WILL NOT BE ISSUED AND QUOTES WILL NOT BE REQUESTED. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC, IHD), intends to award a firm fixed price purchase order on a noncompetitive basis to The MathWorks, Inc. (CAGE: 0C524), located at 3 Apple Hill Dr, Natick, MA 01760, to provide the following service: MatLAB Software License renewals Manufacturer: The MathWorks, Inc. NSWC Indian Head requires renewal of Software Maintenance Service subscriptions for existing perpetual MATLAB licenses and associated toolboxes under Master License 31732211. MATLAB software and maintenance are proprietary to and exclusively provided by The MathWorks, Inc. Only MathWorks can provide authorized updates, patches, and technical support for the existing MATLAB licenses and toolboxes. Alternative sources cannot maintain or support MathWorks proprietary software. Replacing MATLAB would require significant reengineering of legacy code and models, personnel retraining, recertification, schedule delays, and potential disruption to ongoing research and development efforts. Accordingly, renewal directly from The MathWorks, Inc. is necessary to maintain software compatibility, continuity of operations, and access to current updates and technical support. This action is to be undertaken in accordance with FAR 13.106 (b) Soliciting from a single source, on the basis that the vendor is the only known source capable of meeting the government�s requirements. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 513210 for this requirement is. The FSC code is DA10. The resulting contract will be a firm fixed price purchase order. Negotiation being conducted using other than full and open competition procedures pursuant to authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204 (C) (1). This Notice of Intent is NOT a request for quotes. Interested parties may identify their interests and capability to respond to this requirement by November 12, 2026 at 10AM (EST). Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether or whether not to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice.

title: U.S. AFRICOM INDUSTRY DAY - Tunis, Tunisia (2-4 February, 2027)
description: This Special Notice is for market research and planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever, and the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. U.S. Africa Command (USAFRICOM) is seeking interested commercial vendors for targeted Industry Sessions to be held in Tunis, Tunisia. These sessions will take place during the West Africa Shared Security Forum (WASSF) conference scheduled 2 � 4 February 2027. While the main conference has its own agenda, these specific Industry Sessions are a separate, USAFRICOM-hosted opportunity focused on showcasing military technologies, supplies or services available for acquisition by African Partner nations. Selected vendors will be provided with a dedicated space to present their capabilities. They will also be invited to attend the main conference sessions as observers. The logistical details for this specific USAFRICOM Industry Day session are as follows: � Date and Time: 2 February to 4 February 2027 from 08:00 to 17:00 local time � Location: Event location will be provided to selected vendors along with various lobby and foyer spaces adjacent to the conference plenary space. � Provided Space: Open Space for models, displays, and demonstrations. � Permitted Materials: Non-USG provided technologies, super intelligence (AI), and equipment such as drones and unattended sensors, marketing brochures, and operational product samples. Digital presentations on laptops and monitors are permitted. Primary Areas of Interest The U.S. Government is interested in vendors with capabilities in the following fields, though all submissions will be considered: � Geospatial: Drones (UAV/UAS), Commercial GEOINT, Remote Sensing, and Tracking Systems � Command and Control: C4ISR and Airborne C2 Systems � Consulting & Administrative: Systems Integration, Enterprise Architecture, and Acquisition Management � Drones (UAV/UAS) and Counter-UAS: Platforms as well as Counter-UAS and IED detection technologies � Big Data & Software: Intelligence Analytics, Social Media Analysis, Open-Source Intelligence, and Artificial Intelligence � Cyber: Cyber/Info Security, Intrusion Detection, and Vulnerability/Threat Assessment Submission Requirements for Capability Statement Any commercial vendor may submit a Capability Statement and will be considered for participation. The Capability Statement must include the following: � Company Information: Company name, physical address, and primary point of contact (name, title, email, and phone number). � Proposed Exhibit: A detailed description, including any available images or diagrams, of the specific items, technologies, or services you intend to showcase. � Operational Capability in Africa: A comprehensive overview of your company's capabilities and experience within Africa. This must include: � Demonstrated past performance or projects on the continent. � An explanation of your company's ability to operate on the continent. � A brief description of the existing supply chain capable of delivering products and services to African partner nations. Selection and Notification Timeline � Capability Statement Deadline: All interested parties must submit a Capability Statement by email no later than 4:00 PM Central European Time on 12 November 2026. � Government Notification: The U.S. Government will review all submissions and intends to provide a response regarding participation status no later than 15 December 2026 or sooner. � Vendor Acceptance Deadline: Selected vendors shall provide written confirmation of their acceptance of the invitation by 17 December 2026 or sooner. The U.S. Government has final approval of all exhibitor selections to ensure strategic objectives for the conference are met. Conditions for Participation Respondents are advised of the following conditions: � No-Cost to the Government: Exhibitors are responsible for 100% of their costs associated with this event, including but not limited to travel, lodging, visas, and country entry fees. � Logistics and Equipment: Selected vendors are solely responsible for all logistics related to their exhibition space, including the setup/teardown of booths, providing all necessary equipment, and all associated shipping or material handling costs. � No U.S. Government Support: Selection grants access to the event only. No other U.S. Government funding or support will be provided. Points of Contact Please submit all capability statements or any questions regarding this announcement to all points of contact listed below: � christopher.r.conner3.mil@mail.mil � diana.s.bermudez.civ@mail.mil � levi.b.alexis.civ@mail.mil � benjamin.w.wilson4.civ@mail.mil

title: Janitorial Service - Las Vegas, New Mexico
description: The Federal Emergency Management Agency has a requirement for contractor-provided janitorial services at FEMA�s Las Vegas Branch Office in Las Vegas, New Mexico. The contractor will provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, cleaning products, supplies, PPE, and transportation necessary to maintain approximately 13,008 square feet of office space in a clean, sanitary, safe, and professional condition. Services will be available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., from November 17, 2026, through March 16, 2027. title: Incubator Programs for Secure Facilities and Networks at Universities
description: Pursuant to Section 1071 of Public Law 119-60, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (Section 1071), the Department of War (DoW) is conducting an assessment on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits of establishing incubator programs for the development, operation, and sustainment of secure facilities and networks at select institutions of higher education. This RFI seeks detailed information from institutions capable of: Establishing or expanding secure facilities and networks Accelerating the transition of innovative technologies to DoW mission use Increasing availability of secure spaces to support classified research and development (R&D), prototyping, secure collaboration, and research transition activities Expanding the cleared technical workforce Serving as a regional innovation hub supporting multi-tenant use (DoW, industry, and academia) Long-term economic sustainment with significant non-federal cost-sharing The Department intends to use RFI responses to inform its assessment to Congress on the feasibility, advisability, and potential benefits to the Department of establishing the incubator programs described in Section 1071. The purpose of this information request is to ensure that any potential assessment provided to Congress and any subsequently authorized incubator program are grounded in realistic construction, security, governance, and sustainment planning. Early identification of cost, compliance, and institutional commitment factors is intended to reduce risk for both the U.S. Government and participating institutions. This RFI is for planning and assessment purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.

description: This is a Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) RFO 5.101(a) Pre-solicitation notice requirements and (FAR) RFO 12.102 Restricting Competition. This Notice of Intent is for a proposed award of an open market sole source award to EATON CORPORATION for a Service and Preventative Maintenance contract for the following UPS equipment. EATON UPS MODEL 9390-160 - EH456CBC09 9390-160 EE423CAB13 93PM EN493UXX02 93PM EN373UXX02 93PM ES265UXX06 93PM ES262UXX03 93PM ET074UXX02 93PM ES255UXX04 The location of service will be at the Hershel "Woody" Williams VA Medical Center 1540 Spring Valley Drive Huntington, WV 25704-9300. The proposed award is for EATON CORPORATION UEI: NP3NSFVMNUM3. As the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), and an ISO9001 certified supplier, Eaton Corporation (formerly: Eaton Electrical Inc. and Powerware ) is the provider of factory-supported, factory trained, factory authorized and factory certified service for your critical UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) equipment. Eaton offers power quality services for its UPS products, as well as for related equipment such as power distribution units (PDUs), batteries, alternative energy devices and Cutler-Hammer switchgear. Eaton also services products from legacy brands, including Powerware, Exide Electronics, Best Power, IPM, Deltec and Lortec. Eaton is the only authorized provider of service support with the Eaton developed proprietary service software for 3-phase Eaton UPS products. Eaton does not train, certify or support independent third party service providers to deliver or service Eaton UPS and power quality products. Due to its lack of training on competitor s platforms Eaton does not service non-Eaton branded power quality equipment. Eaton only works on its own branded equipment or devices it s been certified to fully support and maintain (e.g., flywheels, static transfer switches). No other service supplier is authorized to possess Eaton proprietary (copyrighted) software, repair documentation, processes or materials. The Period of Performance is for 1 year / 12 months of service. Flex Plan with Two UPS and Two Battery Preventive Maintenance Checks for all 8 systems. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this service is 238210 (Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors). The Product Service Code (PSC) is J061 (Maint/Repair/Rebuild of Equipment- Electric Wire and Power Distribution Equipment). Small business size standard is $19 Million. While this synopsis does not constitute a solicitation, interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to satisfy the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency, by emailing such statement and supporting documentation by NLT 10:00 AM Eastern Time (ET), 11/12/2026 to William Pratt at billie.pratt@va.gov . Please reference the announcement number (36C24527Q0046) in the subject line of the e-mail. Such documentation will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct the procurement on a competitive basis. A determination not to compete this requirement, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government under authorities cited above. See attached: UPS OEM Sourcing Letter Eaton Corp.

title: W099--Sources Sought Bulk Oxygen Rental & Support Services
description: DESCRIPTION The Cincinnati Veterans Administration Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement to provide Temporary Bulk Oxygen Rental & Support Services for Medical Gas Line Repair. The intention of this Sources Sought is to obtain information only. Please do not send a proposal. Requested information: To aid acquisition planning, we re seeking capable and interested firms for the information requested. If your firm meets the criteria please send the point of contract (ronald.heidemann@va.gov) the following, via email: Firm s Name Socio-Economic Status Whether or not your company has a contract vehicle we can order against If your company believes there is an alternative NAICS code please provide this If your company has any questions please provide. 1. Contract Title. Temporary Bulk Oxygen Rental & Support Services for Medical Gas Line Repair 2. Background. Provide a turnkey temporary bulk oxygen supply and services (rental tank, transport, installation, line hookup, controlled shutdown/bleeding, monitoring, and removal) to maintain uninterrupted oxygen service while VA performs a pin hole leak repair in the hospital s piped oxygen system. Work shall comply with VHA Directive 7515(1) and NFPA 99 Health Care Facilities Code requirements for medical gas systems 3. Scope: The Contractor shall furnish all rental equipment, labor, materials, transport, and qualified personnel to: Deliver and set a temporary bulk liquid oxygen (LOX) tank with vaporizers and regulators sized for hospital demand. Connect the temporary supply to the hospital oxygen pipeline (via EOSC/auxiliary connection or source valve), including gauges, check valves, and isolation devices; verify pressure, purity, and flow stability per NFPA 99 Chapter 5. Coordinate and execute a controlled shutdown and bleeding of affected lines, isolate zone valves, and validate alarm behavior with VA Clinical Engineering and Respiratory Therapy. Monitor supply, pressure, and alarms throughout the outage; maintain contingency oxygen cylinders for clinical areas at risk. Support VA repair team during line replacement/brazing and re-qualification (e.g., leak tests, purity checks, pressure verification), then transition back to the permanent bulk system and remove temporary equipment. 4. Specific Tasks : Temporary LOX tank with vaporizers sized to meet peak hourly demand; provide pressure regulating, relief, and check devices; all oxygen service compatible, oil free. Auxiliary/EOSC connection hardware, hoses, and valves compliant with facility EOSC design; include filtration as required. (NFPA 99 2024 emphasizes auxiliary connections for emergency preparedness.) Alarm interface: ensure master and area alarms receive accurate signals during temporary supply (low pressure, source changeover). Performance. Delivery requirements are met: Following VA repair and verification, transition back to primary bulk supply; execute valve re opening sequence, purge procedures, re pressurization, and alarm validation; document test results. Remove temporary equipment and restore site; submit as left drawings, pressure logs, and certification reports if applicable. 6. Place of Performance. Cincinnati VAMC, 3200 Vine Steet, Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 7. Delivery: Cincinnati VAMC 3200 Vine Street Cincinnati Ohio 45220

title: Janitorial Service - Las Vegas, New Mexico
description: Questions and Answers worksheet added as of 11_05_2026. Amended Solicitation adding submission instructions, revised and added clauses. Questions and Answers worksheet added as of 11_04_2026. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has a requirement for contractor-provided janitorial services at FEMA�s Las Vegas Branch Office in Las Vegas, New Mexico. The contractor will provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, cleaning products, supplies, PPE, and transportation necessary to maintain approximately 13,008 square feet of office space in a clean, sanitary, safe, and professional condition. Services will be available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., from November 17, 2026, through March 16, 2027. Required tasks include twice-daily trash removal, restroom and kitchen cleaning, supply replenishment, floor and carpet care, high-touch surface disinfection, and interior and entry-door glass cleaning. Weekly services include detailed stain removal, glass cleaning, and cleaning of baseboards, corners, and other accessible surfaces. A complete deep cleaning, including carpet extraction, is required at the end of the period of performance. The contractor must maintain quality control, promptly correct deficiencies, comply with facility-access and security procedures, and ensure all personnel complete FEMA vetting requirements before beginning work.

description: Questions and Answers worksheet added as of 11_04_2026. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has a requirement for contractor-provided janitorial services at FEMA�s Las Vegas Branch Office in Las Vegas, New Mexico. The contractor will provide all personnel, supervision, equipment, cleaning products, supplies, PPE, and transportation necessary to maintain approximately 13,008 square feet of office space in a clean, sanitary, safe, and professional condition. Services will be available Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., from November 17, 2026, through March 16, 2027. Required tasks include twice-daily trash removal, restroom and kitchen cleaning, supply replenishment, floor and carpet care, high-touch surface disinfection, and interior and entry-door glass cleaning. Weekly services include detailed stain removal, glass cleaning, and cleaning of baseboards, corners, and other accessible surfaces. A complete deep cleaning, including carpet extraction, is required at the end of the period of performance. The contractor must maintain quality control, promptly correct deficiencies, comply with facility-access and security procedures, and ensure all personnel complete FEMA vetting requirements before beginning work.

title: Intent to Sole Source- London Stock Exchange
description: Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC) Procurement, on behalf of The Office of Financial Research (OFR) and the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC), intends to contract with London Stock Exchange Group PLC, 10 Paternoster Square London EC4M 7LS United Kingdom. There is no competitive vendor or regulatory agency that provides these datasets. London Stock Exchange (LSEG) has exclusive rights to the required Masterfile data. On July 21, 2010, President Obama signed the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the "Dodd-Frank Act"), which created the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC) and the Office of Financial Research (OFR). The FSOC is charged with three primary purposes: to identify risks to the financial stability of the United States, to promote market discipline, and to respond to emerging threats to the stability of the U.S. financial system. The FSOC brings together the expertise of federal financial regulators, state regulators, and an insurance expert appointed by the President. The mission of the OFR is to support the Financial Stability Oversight Council (�the Council�) in promoting financial stability by: collecting data on behalf of the Council; providing such data to the Council and member agencies; standardizing the types and formats of data reported and collected; performing applied research and essential long-term research; developing tools for risk measurement and monitoring; performing other related services; making the results of the activities of the OFR available to financial regulatory agencies; and assisting such member agencies in determining the types of formats of data authorized by Dodd-Frank Act to be collected by such member agencies. Pursuant to its mandate, OFR has a Memorandum of Understanding with the Depository Trust and Clearing Corporation (DTCC) for DTCC National Securities Clearing Corporation (NSCC's) ETF PCF Portfolio Data, Historical Data, and Near-Time Supplemental File. This data is provided to OFR from DTCC, however the agreement requires OFR to maintain its own license with the London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) for LSEG�s Stock Exchange Daily Official List (SEDOL) Masterfile�. The SEDOL Masterfile is a unique securities identifier specific to the London Stock Exchange. The OFR and FSOC currently use the proposed contractor�s sole source product for the qFSI monitor and annual report content pursuant to its mission to deliver an annual assessment of the state of the U.S. financial system, as required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information or a copy of the solicitation will not be considered an affirmative response to this Special Notice. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Special Notice will not be accepted. The period of performance for the purchase order is anticipated to be a twelve (12) month base period. TCSC may consider information received no later than 10:00 a.m. EST on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, submitted electronically to TCSCAcquisitionOps@treasury.gov and Brittany.Coffman@treasury.gov, subject: �SS-OFR-27-003 London Stock Exchange- Attn: BCoffman/KZeigler�. All responses must include sufficient evidence that clearly shows your company is capable of providing the content described in this notice. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written response is received by the aforementioned deadline that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet all requirements, and that is more advantageous to the Government, TCSC will make award on a sole source basis to London Stock Exchange Group PLC. Qualified Contractors must provide the following: 1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size (Large Business, Small Business, Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, HUBZone, etc.). Please ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and telephone number, should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 2. UEI Number. 3. Specific details of the product(s) that your company offers in regard to this notice. 4. Whether your content is available through a government contract vehicle or Open Market. 5. A brief capabilities statement (not to exceed 5 pages) that includes a description of your company's standard line of business, as well as a list of customers to whom your company currently provides the specific required content. The following file extensions are not allowable, and application materials/data submitted with these extensions cannot be considered: .bat, .cmd, .com, .exe, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .hta, .cpl, and .zip files. Microsoft Office and Adobe compatible documents are acceptable. No other information regarding this Special Notice will be provided at this time.

title: United Kingdom – Engineering works and construction works – Integrated Partnerships Framework
description: The IF109 Framework is being established to support delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme and will succeed the existing IF105 Integrated Partnerships Framework, which is due to expire in May 2028. The Framework is intended to support delivery of the PC28 investment programme and future regulatory periods whilst securing the capacity, capability, flexibility, value for money and resilience required to deliver NI Water's future capital programme. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework will support a range of works and related services including programme and project management, design, engineering, construction, commissioning and other supporting or ancillary activities necessary to support the successful delivery of NI Water's capital investment programme. The Framework is intended to support delivery of NI Water's future investment priorities, including regulatory compliance, service improvement, resilience enhancement, environmental performance and long-term sustainability objectives. The IF109 Integrated Partnerships Framework comprises four Lots covering: Lot 1 - Minor Civil Pipelaying Works Lot 2 - Minor Civil Works Lot 3 - Minor MEICA & Process Works Lot 4 - Major Civil, MEICA & Process Works Together, these Lots will support the delivery of projects ranging from small-scale network investment and rehabilitation activities through to large-scale, complex, multidisciplinary capital programmes across NI Water's water and wastewater asset base. The Framework has been designed to support long-term delivery of NI Water's investment programme whilst providing the flexibility required to respond to evolving programme, funding and operational requirements throughout its duration. The total framework value may be shared across all Lots.

title: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit
description: JP Murtha Float Mooring Bitts Retrofit - The United States Army Corps of Engineers, (USACE) Pittsburgh District has a requirement for the retrofitting of existing hydraulic structures within an active navigation lock. The Prime Contractor must be capable of executing complex in-the-wet construction, specifically: The John P. Murtha Floating Mooring Bitt Retrofit consists of the installation of Government furnished Floating Mooring Bitts into Contractor fabricated embedded frame on the existing River Chamber Middle Wall. In-the-wet construction methods are required. Design, fabrication, and installation of two dewatering boxes are required for installation of the Floating Mooring Bitts. Removal or alterations to existing work in such a manner as to prevent injury or damage to any portions of the existing work which remain. Repair or replace portions of existing work which have been altered during construction operations to match existing or adjoining work, as approved by the Contracting Officer. At the completion of operations, existing work must be in a condition equal to or better than that which existed before new work started. To achieve this Requirement the Contractor must: a. Floating Plant Operations: Providing, operating, and mooring a fully compliant floating plant (crane/deck barge and push boat) in an active river chamber in accordance with EM 385-1-1. b. Dewatering Box (Cofferdam): Fabricating, installing, and sealing structural steel dewatering boxes against lock monoliths for a strict maximum duration of 90 days. c. Heavy Demolition and Concrete Work: Executing concrete wire-sawing, core drilling, and demolition of existing lock wall recesses, followed by cast-in-place concrete integration. d. Structural Steel and Mooring Bitts: Fabricating heavy steel embedded anchorage frames, and salvaging/installing Government-Furnished Floating Mooring Bitts. e. Commercial Diving: Providing certified commercial dive teams to support underwater inspection, rigging, and cofferdam sealing. The work shall be completed within 730 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed. This acquisition will be procured as an Unrestricted Full and Open Solicitation. The resulting award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Construction Contract. All responsible Bidders are encouraged to participate. The Invitation for Bid (IFB) will be issued on or about 15 September 2026, online through Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) which posts the opportunity to SAM.gov; therefore, requests for hardcopies of the solicitation will not be honored. .The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) for this procurement is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the small business size standard is $45Million.In order to submit a Bid on this project, your company must-1) Be registered in System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain an active registration status. 2) Be registered in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) for the Solicitation Module with the PROPOSAL MANAGER role. System for Award Management (SAM) Registration. Registering in SAM.gov includes both entity validation and entity registration. To register in SAM: a. Navigate to SAM.gov b. Select Sign-In (top right) c. Select Create an Account then Follow the Instructions. d. After Account is Set-up, Select Sign In. e. Under the Entity Management widget, Select Get Started button. f. Select Register Entity. As part of entity registration, a Unique Entity ID will be assigned. title: Y--GRSM 321788 - Oconaluftee River Trail
description: Date: October 28, 2026 To: SAM Federal Business Opportunities From: Rachel Dyer, Contracting Officer, National Park Service, Denver Service Center Subject: Sources Sought Notice Reference: GRSM 321788 - Oconaluftee River Trail This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for the purpose of conducting market research. Proposals are NOT being requested, nor accepted at this time. Responses are being requested from both large and small businesses. Purpose: The purpose of this notice is to gain knowledge regarding the type of interested businesses and their qualifications. The National Park Service (NPS) will use information obtained through this notice to develop an acquisition strategy. The Government anticipates conducting a competitive acquisition for this requirement. The amount of interest or lack thereof will determine the possibility of a small business or other socio-economical small business set-aside for the solicitation. Analysis of the quality of responses to this source sought announcement will be considered in the market research being conducted, and in the making of any small business set-aside determination for this requirement. Additional Information: No proposal package, solicitation, specification or drawings are available with this notice. Cost Reimbursement: Response to this announcement is strictly voluntary; no reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this sources sought announcement or any follow-up information requests. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code: 237310 Small Business Size Standard: $45,000,000.00 Solicitation: The NPS anticipates issuing a request for proposals in the Spring 2027. Bonding: The NPS anticipates bid, performance and payment bonds will be required. Project Description: The National Park Service (NPS) proposes to improve the multi-use Oconaluftee River Trail, that links the gateway community of Cherokee to Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The Oconaluftee River Trail is approximately 8,400 feet, or 1.6 miles, in length and extends from the Oconaluftee Visitor Center to the park boundary with Cherokee, North Carolina. The project corridor is within and/or adjacent to sensitive natural and cultural resources. Preventing or limiting disturbance to and respecting these resources is of high importance to the park. The scope of the work includes, but is not limited to, the following: � Cutting and removal of between 250 to 300 hundred mixed hardwood trees of varying size. Trees can only be felled between November 16 through March 31 of any calendar year. � Widening the trail to approximately 8� in width, adding new aggregate subgrade and paving approximately 8,200 feet of trail with bituminous concrete pavement. � Construction of a new single span steel pedestrian bridge approximately 60 feet in length and 10 feet in clear width, including new stone-faced abutments. � Construction of a new integrally colored concrete multi-use recreational plaza approximately 2800 SF in area, including the construction of stone seating walls and wooden benches. � Construction of approximately 200 linear feet of riverbank erosion utilizing locally harvested vegetation to create a bioengineered fill structure. � Construction of a new "spur" trail to connect the Oconaluftee River Trail to the Saunooke Bridge located on the Big Cove Connector Road. This trail consists primarily of earth cuts and fills and is approximately 250 feet in length. Submittal Contents: Interested (small and large) businesses should submit the following information: (1) Company name, UEI number, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. (2) Business type: Classification as a Large or Small Business under the above listed NAICS, Small Business Administration (SBA) certified Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB), SBA certified Woman Owned Small Business (WOSB), Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned Small Business (EDWOSB). The size of a small business firm includes all parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, etc.�see 13 CFR 121.108.) Misrepresentation of size status can result in penalties. (3) Statement regarding your company�s bonding capacity. Letters from bonding companies are not required at this time. (4) Information demonstrating experience and capability on projects of same or similar size, scope and magnitude, and constructed under similar conditions. (5) In addition businesses may submit existing marketing materials such as capability statements and brochures. (6) UEI Number Only Submittal Due Date/Time: Thursday, November 12, 2026 no later than 9:00am Mountain Time Submit To: Rachel_dyer@ios.doi.gov

title: Refurbish and Repair Equipment Barge #774 - La Crescent, MN (UMRM 702.5)
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District requires a shipyard with a drydock to inspect, refurbish and modify Barge 774, a 110 ft x 26 ft x 5 ft steel equipment barge. Contractor will pick up the barge at Lock and Dam 7 (UMRM 702.5), La Crescent, MN after November 30, transport it to their facility, raise the vessel on a drydock, pressure blast the hull and thoroughly inspect. title: Court Appointed Intermediary Services - Framework Re-Opening October 2026
description: This notice relates to the re-opening of framework agreements originally awarded following a procurement exercise conducted under the light tough regime, following a process similar to the open procedure. The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) is inviting tenders for the provision of Court Appointed Intermediary Services (CAIS), to support vulnerable defendants in the criminal jurisdiction and vulnerable parties and witnesses in the civil, family and tribunal jurisdictions. These services will be provided in courts and tribunals in England and Wales and tribunals in Scotland. Intermediaries facilitate impartial communication to enable complete, coherent and accurate communication between vulnerable people and the courts/tribunals. Intermediaries may be instructed to provide an assessment of a person's communication needs, and provide recommendations on measures that could be put in place by the court to support vulnerable people, young people, children and other individuals who may need assistance during court proceedings. The intermediary may also be required to attend hearings to provide such assistance and support. For the avoidance of doubt, the MoJ is only seeking tenders in relation to intermediary services that currently fall outside the remit of the MoJ Witness Intermediary Scheme (MoJ WIS). All requests for intermediary support for witnesses in criminal cases will continue to be managed via the MoJ WIS. Additional information: The MoJ invites tenders for Court Appointed Intermediary Services to support two existing framework agreements: the Managed & Approved Service Provider framework (MASP), and the Approved Service Provider framework (ASP). The MASP framework seeks providers with the ability to manage multiple simultaneous bookings, and the capability to recruit, train and manage intermediaries to support a range of vulnerabilities, for deployment nationally. The ASP framework seeks experienced and qualified intermediaries to support bookings on demand. There is no limit to the number of service providers awarded a place on either framework, however a service provider may not hold a place on both the MASP and ASP frameworks simultaneously. The MoJ is managing this procurement in accordance with its general obligations under UK law and specifically in accordance with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (PCRs) and the Light Touch Regime contained within Regulations 74 to 77. The framework agreements are dynamic frameworks and a hybrid of a framework agreement and dynamic purchasing system. As such, the framework agreements will be re-opened at six month intervals for the admission of new service providers who qualify against the selection and award criteria outlined in the procurement documents.

description: DESCRIPTION This RFI is solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation or obligation on the part of the Government.? description: The United States Marine Corps requires commercially available television programming and associated commercial television service for authorized Government facilities at MCB Camp Lejeune, MCAS New River, and MCAS Cherry Point. The Government intends to issue a commercial solicitation under Full and Open Competition (Unrestricted) to establish a single-award, firm-fixed-price (FFP) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract under solicitation number M67001-26-Q-0034. Classified under NAICS code 517111 (Wired Telecommunications Carriers) and Product Service Code (PSC) DG11 (IT and Telecom-Network: Telecom Access Services). Services shall be delivered only through existing authorized service points and existing functional interior outlets. The contractor must own, lease, or otherwise have lawful written authority to use all infrastructure, service points, facilities, programming rights, and access authorities needed to provide the ordered service. This requirement does not include cable-drop installation; new interior wiring; repair, replacement, or modification of building wiring; drilling; conduit; pathways; raceways; structural or facility alterations; exterior work; excavation; outside-plant work; or construction of any kind. The contractor shall identify a location as non-serviceable if ordered service cannot be provided through an existing authorized service point and existing functional interior outlet. The acquisition is performance-based. Performance measures include serviceability confirmation, authorized activation, approved programming delivery, outage acknowledgement and restoration, equipment accountability, invoice accuracy, and timely submission of required records.

title: Sources Sought � FY27 Temporary Backup Generator and Transformer Lease and Sustainment � Winn Army Community Hospital, Fort Stewart, Georgia
description: The Department of the Army is conducting market research to identify capable commercial sources for a potential firm-fixed-price service requirement at Winn Army Community Hospital, Fort Stewart, Georgia. The anticipated requirement is for contractor-furnished temporary backup power generation equipment, including a generator and compatible transformer, to support the hospital chiller plant during planned or unplanned power outages. The contractor would provide equipment lease/rental, transition or installation as required, testing and commissioning, 24/7 operational readiness, preventive and corrective maintenance, monitoring, emergency response, and removal/decommissioning at the end of performance. The Government seeks input regarding available commercial solutions, transition approach, equipment availability, schedule, pricing structure, and small-business capability. This notice is for market-research purposes only and is not a solicitation or commitment to award. The Government has not determined whether existing temporary-power equipment will be available to a successor contractor. Respondents should address their ability to sustain an existing system, if lawfully made available, and to provide a replacement system if necessary. Attachment: A Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached for market-research reference. The draft PWS is preliminary, subject to revision, and provided solely to assist interested parties in assessing capability. It is not a solicitation, request for quotation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government. Respondents are encouraged to identify any requirements that may unnecessarily restrict competition and recommend commercially reasonable alternatives.

title: CDC Typefi Orion Cloud Teams Software Licenses and Implementation
description: NOTICE OF INTENT (NOI) � Typefi Orion Cloud Teams Software Licenses and Implementation Product Service Code (PSC): 7A21 NAICS Code: 541519 Place of Performance: Online software access supporting CDC, Atlanta, GA 30329-4018 Solicitation Number: 75D301-27-Q-79332 Description This is a Notice of Intent, not a separate request for quote. The Government�s solicitation for this requirement is provided through the associated combined synopsis/solicitation. The Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), on behalf of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Center for Emerging and Zoonotic Infectious Diseases (NCEZID), Office of the Director (OD), intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract to Typefi Systems, Inc. for Typefi Orion Cloud Teams software licenses, implementation services, and support. The purpose of this requirement is to replace the Emerging Infectious Diseases (EID) journal�s legacy eXtyles editorial-production software and support its manuscript editing, reference validation, metadata preparation, and publication-production workflows. According to Typefi�s November 3, 2026 sole-source letter, eXtyles has been discontinued by its owner, John Wiley & Sons (Wiley). The requirement includes 12 Typefi Orion Cloud Teams user licenses, onboarding and implementation services, a Wiley royalty, training, and technical support. Required capabilities include Orion for Word/Server integration; SmartReplace for automated editorial cleanup; SmartReference for reference validation, correction, and duplicate-reference checking; Harvard-to-Vancouver citation conversion; PubMed and CrossRef deposit capabilities; and JATS XML export. These capabilities support preparation of author-created Microsoft Word documents for publication, including application of editorial styles, automated rule-based edits, validation of references and citations, and production of structured XML for EID�s publishing workflow. The anticipated base period of performance is November 18, 2026, through November 17, 2027. The requirement also includes four annual subscription option periods, exercisable at the Government�s discretion. Justification for Single Source Typefi Systems, Inc. is the proposed single source for Typefi Orion licenses, implementation services, and support. The requirement supports migration from EID�s legacy eXtyles editorial-production software while preserving compatibility with existing editorial configurations and publishing requirements. In its November 3, 2026 sole-source letter, Typefi Systems, Inc. states that the Typefi group of companies developed Orion and owns its intellectual property. Typefi Systems, Inc. holds the exclusive license to sell Orion in the Americas. The letter further states that no unaffiliated reseller, distributor, or other third party is authorized to sell Orion. Typefi also states that Orion is the only solution authorized by Wiley to import existing eXtyles data and configurations, including Auto-Redact dictionaries, article types, metadata, paragraph styles, and citation settings. Typefi holds an exclusive license from Wiley for the eXtyles source code. Orion integrates with Typefi�s Edifix reference-processing service to format, correct, and link references against CrossRef and PubMed. According to Typefi, Edifix uses the same reference-processing engine that powered eXtyles, supporting consistency during migration. Edifix itself is available to other products through a third-party application programming interface and is not asserted to be exclusive to Orion. The proposed acquisition addresses EID�s requirement for the combined editorial automation, authorized migration, reference-processing, and JATS XML export capabilities described above. Authority This acquisition is being conducted under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, including FAR 12.102(a), as implemented by applicable HHS FAR Overhaul deviations. For acquisitions valued at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, the Contracting Officer must document the decision that only one source is available and the basis for that decision. Submission of Capability Statements Interested parties capable of providing the same or similar products or services must submit a capability statement electronically. Responses will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements must demonstrate the ability to provide Typefi Orion Cloud Teams licenses and associated services or an equivalent solution capable of meeting the Government�s editorial-production requirements. Responses must address support for 12 users; Microsoft Word/Server integration; automated editorial cleanup; reference validation, correction, and duplicate-reference checking; Harvard-to-Vancouver citation conversion; PubMed and CrossRef deposit capabilities; and JATS XML export. Capability statements must also explain the proposed approach to migrating existing eXtyles data and configurations, maintaining compatibility with EID�s editorial-production workflow, and providing implementation, training, and ongoing technical support. Respondents proposing Typefi Orion must provide evidence of authorization to supply the required licenses and services. This procurement is subject to FAR 52.232-18 Availability of Funds (APR 1984) Funds are not presently available for this contract. The Government�s obligation under this contract is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds from which payment for contract purposes can be made. No legal liability on the part of the Government for any payment may arise until funds are made available to the Contracting Officer for this contract and until the Contractor receives notice of such availability, to be confirmed in writing by the Contracting Officer. description: The Department of the Army is conducting market research to identify capable commercial sources for a potential firm-fixed-price service requirement at Winn Army Community Hospital, Fort Stewart, Georgia. The anticipated requirement is for contractor-furnished temporary backup power generation equipment, including a generator and compatible transformer, to support the hospital chiller plant during planned or unplanned power outages. The contractor would provide equipment lease/rental, transition or installation as required, testing and commissioning, 24/7 operational readiness, preventive and corrective maintenance, monitoring, emergency response, and removal/decommissioning at the end of performance. The Government seeks input regarding available commercial solutions, transition approach, equipment availability, schedule, pricing structure, and small-business capability. This notice is for market-research purposes only and is not a solicitation or commitment to award. The Government has not determined whether existing temporary-power equipment will be available to a successor contractor. Respondents should address their ability to sustain an existing system, if lawfully made available, and to provide a replacement system if necessary. The draft PWS is preliminary, subject to revision, and provided solely to assist interested parties in assessing capability. It is not a solicitation, request for quotation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government. Respondents are encouraged to identify any requirements that may unnecessarily restrict competition and recommend commercially reasonable alternatives.

description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 10 of 10 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 10 This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY.� It is neither a solicitation nor a request for quote (RFQ) and it does not obligate the Government to award a contract.� Request for solicitation will not receive a response.� The Government will not pay nor reimburse any costs of preparing this response.� The source s sought notice is for market research purposes to make the appropriate acquisition decision and gain knowledge of potential qualified businesses and their Small Business Administration (SBA) size classification in relation to North America Industry Classification System (NAICS) 333922, Conveyor and Conveying Equipment Manufacturing with an associated size standard of 500 employees. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 8 Orlando Contracting Team is seeking interested sources to remove the existing hospital garment conveyor system and provide a turnkey solution to replace the garment conveyor system for the Orlando VA Medical Center (OVAMC). See attached documentation to see the salient characteristics. If your business can meet or exceed the requirement, please provide a capability statement. The capability statement shall be limited to no more than five pages and must clearly state the following: Capability in industry to manufacture or provide the required Garment Conveyor System with Inventory Management Capability. Offerors who cannot provide historical information from their company regarding the outlined attachment or similar scope and scale should provide corresponding information to show how the company would meet the OVAMC requirements. This information should provide level of confidence in the Government that an offeror would meet or exceed the delivery requirements to provide the required product. The automated hospital garment conveyor system shall meet the following minimum characteristics: 2.1 Automated Hospital Garment Conveyor System The garment conveyor system shall be fabricated from heavy-duty steel construction suitable for continuous institutional healthcare use. The system should provide a minimum storage capacity of 2,200 garments. The system shall operate as a standalone, self-contained system. The system shall not require connection to a hospital network, internet service, cloud service, external database, or other network infrastructure for normal operation. The system should provide current inventory status and reporting capabilities. All operational and inventory data shall be stored locally within the system. The system shall fit within the existing two-level garment storage room. First-floor equipment footprint shall not exceed 230 inches (L) × 128 inches (W). A minimum of 60 inches of clear employee workspace and access aisle clearance shall be maintained. Second-floor equipment footprint shall not exceed 210 inches (L) × 128 inches (W) × 84 inches (H). The system shall fit within the available space without requiring structural modifications to the building. The conveyor system shall be capable of operating in both forward and reverse directions. The system shall include a dedicated manual directional control lever or equivalent operator control that allows authorized personnel to reverse conveyor movement as required for loading, unloading, maintenance, troubleshooting, or garment retrieval operations. The directional control shall be readily accessible to operators and shall function without requiring access to software configuration menus or administrative settings. Operation of the forward and reverse functions shall not adversely affect inventory tracking accuracy or system safety features. The conveyor system shall include safety interlocks and emergency stop devices that remain fully functional during both forward and reverse operations. Directional changes shall be performed in accordance with the manufacturer's safety requirements and operating procedures. . 2.2 Inventory Management Solution The inventory management solution shall operate on a dedicated desktop computer provided as part of the system. All software and firmware updates shall be performed locally at the workstation without internet connectivity. The software should function independently of the hospital network, internet connection, cloud services, or external databases. The inventory management solution shall operate as a standalone system. The solution should not require connectivity to the hospital network, internet, cloud services wireless networks, or external databases for normal operation. The system shall maintain an accurate inventory count of all garments stored within the conveyor system. The system should track garment storage locations and retrieval locations. The system shall automatically update inventory records when garments are added, removed, or relocated Historical inventory information shall be retained locally within the system. The system should provide inventory reporting capability directly from the operator interface. Authorized users shall be able to view current inventory status and transaction history. Reports should identify garment quantities and storage locations. 2.3 Additional requirements All system components, including conveyors, carousels, controls, motors, inventory management equipment, operator workstations, support structures, and associated accessories, shall fit entirely within the available room dimensions specified in this solicitation. The proposed system should not require modifications to load-bearing walls, floors, ceilings, columns, roof structures, or other structural building elements. The contractor shall verify all field dimensions prior to fabrication and installation. The contractor shall provide a layout drawing demonstrating compliance with all dimensional requirements, required employee workspaces, maintenance access areas, and aisle clearances. The installed system shall maintain all required safety, fire protection, operational, and maintenance access clearances. Any utility connections required for system operation shall utilize existing building infrastructure or minor non-structural modifications only. 3. Contractor is shall: 3.1 Remove existing conveyor system Disconnect, dismantle, remove, and properly dispose of the existing garment conveyor system, including all associated tracks, supports, motors, controls, wiring, hardware, and accessories. Remove all equipment, mounting hardware, anchors, fasteners, and components associated with the existing system. Repair any damage resulting from removal activities and restore affected areas to their original condition or better, in accordance with Facility Management Service (FMS) requirements. All holes, penetrations, mounting points, anchors, wall openings, floor openings, and ceiling penetrations created or exposed during removal shall be properly repaired and sealed using materials that match existing construction and finishes. Any damaged walls, floors, ceilings, paint, coatings, or other building surfaces affected by the removal process shall be repaired and restored to match adjacent existing conditions. All restoration work shall be subject to review and acceptance by the Facility Management Service (FMS) prior to final project acceptance. The contractor shall remove all debris, waste materials, and discarded equipment from the site and maintain a clean and safe work area throughout the project. Upon completion of removal activities, the area shall be left clean, fully restored, and ready for installation of the new garment conveyor system. 3.2 Provide Turnkey Installation Furnish all labor, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, supervision, permits, licenses, and incidental items necessary to provide a complete, fully operational garment conveyor system. Provide and install all conveyor equipment, tracks, carousels, motors, controls, support structures

PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This project adds electrical distribution infrastructure and fiber optic communications infrastructure to the existing base networks, supporting multiple new projects associated with the bed-down of the B-21 weapons system at Dyess Air Force Base with an estimated Construction Cost Limitation of $28,550,000. The communications component of this project includes the addition of single mode fiber optic cable in underground concrete encased duct, together with telephone system expansion. title: B21 Utilities & Site Improvements, Communications & Electrical Infrastructure, Dyess AFB OT Feasibility & Business Feedback
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought Notice/RFI � B-21 Utilities & Site Improvements, Communications and Electrical Infrastructure, Dyess AFB, Texas DISCLAIMER: This Sources Sought (SS) is for planning and market research purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP) or an Invitation for Bids (IFB). This notice is issued under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a (Other Transaction Authority for Construction and Repair) and is not subject to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). No solicitation is available at this time. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. PROJECT DESCRIPTION This project adds electrical distribution infrastructure and fiber optic communications infrastructure to the existing base networks, supporting multiple new projects associated with the bed-down of the B-21 weapons system at Dyess Air Force Base with an estimated Construction Cost Limitation of $28,550,000. The communications component of this project includes the addition of single mode fiber optic cable in underground concrete encased duct, together with telephone system expansion. The electrical distribution component includes power cabling, also in underground concrete encased duct, as well as pole mounted power conductors and all associated transformers & equipment. Primary Underground Distribution includes new switchgear, cabling, duct banks, manholes & other associated appurtenances. Facilities to be designed as permanent construction in accordance with Department of Defense Unified Facilities Criteria 1-200-01, General Building Requirements. This project will comply with Department of Defense antiterrorism/force protection requirements per Unified Facility Criteria 4-010-01, Department of Defense Minimum Antiterrorism Standards for Buildings, and Unified Facility Criteria 4-010-06, Cybersecurity of Facility-Related Control Systems. INSTRUCTIONS TO INDUSTRY Review Attached Project Information Packet (PIP): Interested firms are directed to review the attached document. This packet provides comprehensive project requirements, constraints, and the complete questionnaire reference. title: H365--ANNUAL MEDICAL GAS TESTING POP: 12/01/2026 - 09/30/2031
description: 36C26227Q0022 ******* The purpose of this amendment is to: 1. Respond to questions asked regarding this solicitation. 2. Change the Period of Performance (POP) start date from 11/20/2026 to 12/01/2026. Base: 12/01/2026 09/30/2027 OY 1: 10/01/2027 09/30/2028 OY 2: 10/01/2028 09/30/2029 OY 3: 10/01/2029 09/30/2030 OY 4: 10/01/2030 09/30/2031 3. Change the response due date from 11/09/2026 to 11/12/2026. Questions and Answers: Q. Can you please let me know the total number of outlets to be tested.� A. 3,000 Total. Q. # vacuum inlets A. 3,000 Q. # of medical gas system source equipment & location Bulk Oxygen, Med air, Vacuum, Nitrogen, WAGD, Dental Air, Dental Vacuum, Carbon Dioxide. Locations Main Hospital and Building 32 (cancer center) Q. # of medical gas booms/columns A. 38, Please see attachment named BOOM INVENTORY . Q. Could you please clarify whether the prime contractor must independently hold the ASSE 6020 Medical Gas Inspector and ASSE 6030 Medical Gas Verifier certifications, or whether these requirements can be satisfied through a qualified subcontractor whose personnel possess the required certifications? A. ASSE 6020 and ASSE 6030 certifications are required. Q. What are the manufacturer, model, and serial number of the boom equipment, source equipment, vacuum and air system? At a minimum, we need a manufacturer, model #, serial number for each system and each motor/compressor. Would providing photos of the source equipment be possible? A. We do not have the serial numbers or photos of the boom equipment but please see Exell spreadsheet attached Boom Inventory which has the Make, Model and location. Q. The Government provide the most recent annual medical gas inspection report, or an inventory showing quantities of outlets/inlets by gas type, zone valve boxes, area alarm panels, master alarm panels and source equipment? A. No, we cannot provide the inspection report but we are providing the boom inventory. Please see Exell spreadsheet attached Boom Inventory . Q. Can the Government provide the most recent annual medical gas inspection report, or an inventory showing quantities of outlets/inlets by gas type, zone valve boxes, area alarm panels, master alarm panels and source equipment? A. No Q. If this is a follow-on requirement, what is the prior contract number? A. Prior Contract No. : 36C26222C0020 Q. Which gases and systems are in scope (oxygen, medical air, vacuum, nitrous oxide, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, WAGD, instrument air)? A. Please refer to statement of work section V. Scope Q. Is the bulk oxygen tank owned and maintained by the gas supplier, with the contractor s scope limited to the pipeline side? A. The bulk oxygen is owned and maintained by the supplier. Q. Are Category 3 systems, such as dental air and vacuum, in scope? A. Yes Q. Does the Government expect only annual periodic inspection and testing, or a full NFPA 99 system verification each year? A. Only Annual. Q. Does each annual CLIN cover a single inspection event per year? A. Yes Q. May the ASSE 6020 and 6030 credentials be held by subcontractor personnel instead of the prime s employees? A. Certs. Must be held by the prime and subcontractor. Q. Must the field team include both a 6020 inspector and a 6030 verifier, or is credential acceptable for annual testing? A. Yes Q. Should pricing assume evening or weekend work for the ICU, OR, SICU and ED zones? A. Yes. Q. If a master alarm sensor is not on a demand check fitting, will the VA allow a brief isolation to test it, or is that test excluded? A. Yes, a brief moment. Q. Are photos required for every outlet/inlet, or only for sources, alarm panels, zone valves and deficiencies? A. Only deficiencies. Q. How many particulate and dewpoint sample points are expected, based on the number of floors in the Main Hospital and Buildings 30, 31 and 32? A. No. This test will only to be performed for installation,� repair, or modification of any medical gas piping systems, Building 29, 30 has no medical gas. Q. When was the last annual inspection done, and when was the first inspection due under this contract? A. The last inspection was completed on 11/24/25 - 2026 inspection needs to be completed before 12/21/26. Q. Oxygen particulate analysis: This filter test is typically performed as a pre-test during construction projects under NFPA 99. The results would generally be expected to remain unchanged unless the pipeline is breached during construction. Please confirm whether this test is required as part of the annual inspection. A. No particulate test performed during verification of newly installed or modified medical gas piping systems only. Q. ASSE 6010 certification: Please confirm whether ASSE 6010 certification is required. Our understanding is that this is a medical gas installer certification, rather than an annual inspection requirement under NFPA 99. A. No, only if repairs need to be performed, contractor shall be 6010 certified to make repairs. Q. Boom testing frequency: Please confirm whether boom testing is required annually. Our understanding is that NFPA 99 recommends testing every 18 months. A. VA requires this test to be performed annually. Q. Boom testing scope: Please confirm whether the testing includes disassembly of the booms to inspect for leaks and dry rot. A. Yes Q. Boom testing report: Please confirm whether the detailed report should include photographs of disassembled booms and a comprehensive list of recommended repairs. A. Yes, if any deficiencies are found. Q. Building confirmation: Mr. Stockman indicated that Eye Clinic Building 32 and Audiology Building 30 should be excluded from the proposal. Please confirm. A. Only main Hospital and building 31 (cancer center) will be tested annually. Q. Could you please clarify what repair work, if any, must be included in the annual fixed price? Specifically, should the contractor include any routine repairs or corrective maintenance, or will all repairs, replacement parts, and installation services be treated as separately authorized work under Section VI? A. This solicitation is only for Inspection, not for repairs. In the Statement of Work (Section VII) we have to include "Over and Above Repair" to clarify that the contractor must notify the POC immediately if any repairs needs to be made.
